title: Inertia of a pair bound through the field

key_results.statement: In the sector $P$ (body 1 as representative, continued to real $P$) the band contract at order $\tau^2$ is the relative chain $h_P$ with bond amplitudes $t(\rho;P)=\kappa_1(\rho)e^{-2iP}+\kappa_2(\rho)$; $r$ even and $r$ odd form separate rings.
At leading order in $\varepsilon$, $M^{(2)}(r)=-2ng_1g_2\ell(r)/t_f$ and the relative potential is $V(r)=\frac{ng_1g_2}{t_fL}r(L-r)$: a well at contact for $g_1g_2>0$, a hill for $g_1g_2<0$.

Under R and B, for every branch combination and both signs of $\gamma_1\gamma_2$, bound levels exist: the lowest relative levels if $\sigma_1\sigma_2\gamma_1\gamma_2>0$, the highest if $<0$; the extreme level is of one sign (bodies near $p_i=0$) if $s_\beta=\mathrm{sgn}[g_1g_2(\mu_1^{-1}+\mu_2^{-1})]=+1$ and alternating (bodies near $p_1=-p_2=\pm\pi/2$) if $s_\beta=-1$; excited levels have nodes.

open_issues: The code sets do not meet B4 for the mark terms (|ρ_L| = 0.6–12% against |D^mark| ≈ 0.2–0.3% of 1/E_b''); the code checks (6.6) with the ring term included.
The closed forms (6.2), (6.4), (6.15), (6.17) use the second-order mutual term; at η≈0.3 the exact binding slope is about half of F; statements in terms of β_ν, b_ν and M are unaffected.
The O(ε³) remainder of (6.7) is large at moderate couplings (ratio 1.40 for (a), −0.19 for (c) at η≈0.3), so the mark part is reliable only for small η.

The O(ε) corrections of (6.13), (6.14) from the second-order weights are not evaluated (the bond function B of (4.7) is not quoted); in the code 13–16% in the weight differences and up to 50% in the acceleration for set C, where g_1+g_2 is small against |g_i|.
On the ring, (6.13) has a g_s-independent part from the relative cut r=L/2 (up to 0.6% of the first-order part in set A); it is not bounded analytically.
In tight binding of the even class β_0∼1/χ and B3 fails when χ ≳ δ_1δ/τ'²; likewise near the sign change of β_ν of excited levels; the order-τ⁴ band contract is then needed.
For σ_i=+1 and N_f>1 the field excitation energies near 2R_i become dense and the windows of (6.15) shrink; whether weakly coupled resonances can be tolerated is open.

The family with an equality in (6.17)(ii) needs very large rings (L*_0 ∝ M²/(τ²χ^{1/3})), rests on the stated orders of the remainders of (6.7) and (6.9), and was checked only on the leading-order line chain.
Out of scope: full grip, tori, highest field state, bodies of one type, the speed of a front of the field, and how typical the structure is.

Tight binding χ→∞: even class E_b''≈s_e·8κ̄_1κ̄_2/F and odd class 1/E_b''=2s_β(μ_1+μ_2), equal to direct perturbation of the contact states
